newsitem.title: CHILE: Chile shares slump at close, search for support.
newsitem.headline: Chile shares slump at close, search for support.

text.p: Chilean blue chips skidded to close more than one percent lower with the market dragged below its previous support level by sharp falls in Chilean-issued ADRs, said traders.
Stocks are seen tumbling further at the opening on concerns that the Federal Reserve will raise U.S. interest rates at its meeting on March 25, they said.
The 40-share index ended down 1.34 percent at 113.03 points. The general index lost 0.81 percent to 5,257.58 points.
Turnover rose to 10.9 billion pesos from nine billion pesos on Monday.
The bolsa crumpled under the pressure of Wall Street's sell-off, with Chilean blue chips plunging below their previous level of 114 points.
"The market will be looking for support in the next couple of days and could settle around 110-112 points," said one dealer.

Leading decliners included supermarket chain Santa Isabel which dropped after investors reacted negatively to the company's explanation of its 1996 earnings during a conference call with analysts, said dealers.
Investors were disappointed by the firm's fourth quarter operating earnings, which were weaker than they had been expecting, they said.
Santa Isabel dropped 6.06 percent to 728 pesos.
Other losers included copper products maker Madeco, down 4.46 percent at 1,070 pesos and steel producer Cap which shed 1.85 percent to 1,060 pesos.
Winners included juice company Jucosa, up 4.23 percent at 18.25 pesos and airline LanChile which rose 0.93 percent to 545 pesos.
